column5: Send notifications from this device and extensions to the watch
column13: The master switch for everything forwarded. Off drops notifications before they reach the watch; incoming calls and firmware prompts use their own path and still arrive, as do notifications matching an "Always allow" filter. For a short break use Mute temporarily on the Alerts tab.

column3: Only when the screen is off or locked
column5: Hold notifications back while you use this device
column13: While the display is on and the session unlocked, notifications stay here instead of also buzzing your wrist. Urgent ones and "Always allow" filter matches still go through, and calls ring as usual. Without a graphical login stoandl can't tell, so everything is forwarded.

column5: Link this device's Do Not Disturb with the watch's Quiet Time
column13: Desktop → watch turns on the watch's Quiet Time when you enable Do Not Disturb here; Watch → desktop does the reverse; Both ways keeps them in step. GNOME/Phosh and Plasma are detected automatically. Only manual Quiet Time is mirrored, not its schedules.

column5: Also send missed notifications up to this old (minutes)
column13: When the watch comes back, it also gets notifications it missed within this window. Nothing from before stoandl started or the watch was paired is sent, and nothing the watch already has. 0 sends only what arrives after the reconnect.

column5: Where the sending app's name appears on a notification
column13: Small line puts it in small print under the title; Subtitle uses the large bold line unless the source brings its own subtitle; Off leaves it out. It is never shown twice. Each app can override this on the Alerts tab.

column5: Show photos and screenshots that notifications carry
column13: On Pebble Time 2 and Round 2 (firmware 4.35+), a picture attached to a notification is sent along; sender avatars never are. At most 32 are kept on this device and deleted with their notification; turning this off deletes them all. Single apps can be excluded on the Alerts tab.

column5: The reply choices the watch offers
column13: Used for notifications that accept replies: extension messages without their own list, and Plasma desktop notifications with the reply patch. Empty uses the watch's own list. The watch takes 512 bytes in total, so the end of a long list is dropped.

column5: Open the app on this device from the watch (Plasma)
column13: Adds Open to notifications that do something when clicked; choosing it does what clicking the popup would. GNOME does not let another program click a notification, so it never appears there.

column5: Remove from the watch what you dismissed on this device
column13: A notification closed here, read in its app, or closed by an extension disappears from the watch too. A popup that merely timed out into the history stays.

column5: Remember each app so it can be muted or styled
column13: Every app that notifies gets an entry on the Alerts tab (mute, vibration, icon, colour, app name, pictures), and the watch offers a Mute action. Muted notifications are dropped on this device. Off treats every app the same.

column5: Mute state an app gets the first time it notifies
column13: Choose Muted to opt apps in one by one. Apps already in the list keep their own setting.

column5: Apps whose notifications the watch's call screen replaces
column13: While a call rings or is in progress, these apps' notifications are held back because the watch shows its own call screen; Missed call still arrives. Their title also names the caller when the number isn't in your contacts. "calls" is GNOME Calls; Plasma Mobile's Phone app needs no entry.

column5: vCard files or folders used to name incoming callers
column13: Numbers are matched on their last digits, so +49… and 0… forms both work; folders are searched recursively. The default is Plasma Mobile's address book. Nothing leaves this device.

column5: stoandl's own warnings and prompts
column13: Pairing problems, Bluetooth blocked, an extension to set up, a permission request or a fully charged watch. Permission prompts and the full-battery message also appear on the watch. Off only hides them; problems are still logged and in support bundles. Firmware update messages have their own switch.

column5: A watch keeps dropping, or its pairing was removed
column13: Shown when a watch connects and drops straight away (usually unpaired on the watch) or its pairing was removed here, with a Re-pair or Pair button.

column5: Another app's Bluetooth search stops reconnecting
column13: A program searching for devices, often an open Bluetooth settings page, can hog the adapter so the watch can't reconnect.

column5: An installed extension can't start yet, or keeps crashing
column13: Shown when an extension needs settings before it can run, or was stopped after repeated crashes. Open Apps → Extensions.

column5: Allow or deny an app's request on the watch and here
column13: With plugins on, an app that needs approval shows Allow and Deny on the watch and here. Off: no prompt appears and the app is refused until you answer in its permissions or with `stoandl perms`.

column5: When a watch on the charger reaches 100 %
column13: Once per charge; re-arms at 97 % or below. Classic-era watches report hourly, so it can be up to an hour late.

column5: Bluetooth can't search while you pair
column13: Shown once per pairing attempt when discovery keeps failing to start, so no watch can be found. The pairing status reports it either way.

column3: Send the app list to the watch
column5: For future firmware with per-app settings on the watch
column13: Copies the per-app list and mute states into the watch's database, as the official app does. Current PebbleOS has no screen for it, so this normally changes nothing; muting works here either way.

column5: Send forecasts to the watch's Weather app
column13: Forecasts come from Open-Meteo (free, no account) for the places below; nothing is fetched until a place exists. Off stops these fetches and the pins but keeps your places. Weather for classic watchfaces and Name places from coordinates have their own switches and keep working.

column5: Fixed places, as Name:latitude:longitude
column13: For example Berlin:52.52:13.405; the name is what the watch shows. Use the search below to add one without coordinates. The first place is the main one (sunrise and sunset pins) unless Current location is on.

column5: Search a city to add it
column13: Turns on the search box below and `stoandl weather search`. Only the text you type is sent, and only when you search.

column5: Add weather for where you are, via the location service
column13: Adds a place that follows you, found by GeoClue at city level (usually Wi-Fi and cell towers). It is shown first and updated on every refresh. GeoClue must allow stoandl: a location agent asks you, or allow the app id under Apps & plugins → Advanced.

column5: Look up town names for coordinates
column13: Turns the current location, and coordinates that classic watchfaces ask about, into a town name. Off by default because it sends your position to a third-party service; without it the watch shows the label under Advanced.

column5: Add them to the watch's timeline
column13: Pins for today and the next two days for the main place, with the other places in the details, as the original app did.

column5: Answer old watchfaces whose weather service shut down
column13: Many 2014–2016 faces ask Yahoo or OpenWeatherMap 2.5, which no longer answer, so they show "--". stoandl answers instead, from Open-Meteo, as the official app does. Most such faces also need Location for watchapps.

column5: How often forecasts are fetched (minutes)
column13: When a watch connects, weather is refetched only if it is older than this. Shorter is fresher but means more requests and wake-ups; on a sleeping phone a due refresh runs at the next wake.

column5: Add places from your desktop's weather app
column13: GNOME Weather reads places saved in GNOME/Phosh Weather. A command runs the program below, one Name:lat:lon line per place. Imported places are re-read on every refresh. Plasma keeps no coordinates.

column5: Prints one Name:lat:lon line per place
column13: Runs on every refresh, as you, without a sandbox. If it calls a web geocoder, that request is one you chose.

column5: Shown when no place name is looked up
column13: The name the watch shows for the current location when name lookup is off or finds nothing.

column5: Put upcoming events on the watch's timeline
column13: Events from yesterday to a week ahead become timeline pins, with reminders if on. Needs a source: local calendars found automatically, or accounts and feeds you add. Off removes the calendar pins until turned back on.
column16: the CalDAV and iCal servers you add

column5: Use calendars stored on this device
column13: Looks for .ics calendars your desktop keeps: Calindori on Plasma Mobile, ~/.calendars and ~/calendars. Nothing leaves this device. Online calendars are added under Accounts and feeds.

column5: The watch buzzes before events
column13: Uses each event's own reminders. Off keeps the pins but the watch stays quiet.

column5: Vibration pattern for calendar reminders
column13: Watch default uses the watch's own pattern. Your own patterns appear here too.

column5: Keep invitations you declined on the timeline
column13: Off hides them. Turn on to see your full schedule.

column5: How often calendars are checked for changes (minutes)
column13: Local files are picked up when they change anyway; this mainly sets how often CalDAV accounts and iCal links are fetched, and moves the timeline window forward.

column5: Control media players from the watch
column13: Works with any MPRIS player (most Linux players and browsers). Nothing leaves this device.

column5: System volume or the player's own volume
column13: System volume works like the device's volume keys; Player volume changes only the playing app, which not every player supports.

column5: Next and previous jump 15 s in podcasts and audiobooks
column13: In a player that can seek but has no next or previous track, the watch's buttons jump 15 seconds. Off: they always skip tracks.

column5: Replaces the detected system volume tool
column13: By default stoandl finds wpctl, pactl or amixer. Set both commands to use your own; each runs once per button press.

column5: Replaces the detected system volume tool
column13: Both commands must be set to take effect.

column5: Turn what you say into the watch into text
column13: Used for voice replies, dictation in watchapps and voice notes from extensions. Local model runs on this device (a few seconds of CPU per dictation); Custom command runs your own engine; HTTP service sends the recording to an OpenAI-compatible server.
column16: the speech-to-text server set under Advanced (HTTP service only)

column5: The downloaded model Local model runs
column13: Download one below; bigger models are more accurate but slower. Parakeet v3 understands many languages.

column5: The language you speak, or auto
column13: A code such as en or de helps engines that guess badly. Passed to a custom command as {lang} and to the HTTP service.

column5: Tried when the first isn't ready, fails or is too slow
column13: Also used when the first hears nothing. The watch waits 14 s for a dictation, so with a second engine the first gets 7 of them.
column16: the speech-to-text server set under Advanced (HTTP service only)

column5: Read assistant answers aloud on the watch speaker
column13: Needs a watch with a speaker (Pebble Time 2, Pebble 2 Duo). Local model runs Piper or espeak-ng on this device; Custom command runs your own engine; HTTP service sends the text to an OpenAI-compatible speech server. The watch's speaker volume and mute apply.
column16: the speech server set under Advanced (HTTP service only)

column5: A downloaded Piper voice, or espeak-ng
column13: Download voices below; "low" voices are enough for the watch speaker and fastest. espeak-ng needs no download and speaks every language, but sounds robotic.

column5: 100 % is normal speed
column13: Applied as Piper's length scale, espeak's words per minute, or the HTTP speed field.

column5: Prints the text spoken in {wav}
column13: Runs for each dictation with {wav} (16 kHz mono WAV) and {lang}; whatever it prints is the text. See docs/voice.md.

column5: OpenAI-compatible transcription URL
column13: For example whisper-server, speaches or LocalAI on this device or your network, or a hosted service. Each recording is sent here.

column5: Model name, if the server needs one
column13: Sent as the model field, for example whisper-1.

column5: Kept out of stoandl.conf (keyring, else a private file)
column13: Sent as a Bearer token. Left out of backups.

column5: Save each dictation as a WAV file, for troubleshooting
column13: Recordings go to ~/.cache/stoandl/voice. They contain your voice: turn this off and delete the folder when done.

column5: Reads text on stdin, writes a WAV file to stdout
column13: For engines installed by hand (Kokoro, sherpa-onnx, RHVoice). {lang} is replaced by the language.

column5: OpenAI-compatible /v1/audio/speech URL
column13: Each answer's text is sent here. Speaches, LocalAI or openedai-speech can run Piper or Kokoro on a computer on your network; hosted services charge per character.

column5: For example tts-1
column13: Leave empty for servers that ignore it.

column5: For example alloy
column13: Leave empty for the server's default.

column5: Kept out of stoandl.conf (keyring, else a private file)
column13: Separate from the speech-to-text key so a key is never sent to a server it wasn't meant for. Empty sends no key.

column5: Ask the watch for steps, sleep and heart rate on connect
column13: On each connection stoandl asks for data newer than what it already has (the very first time that is everything), but not again within 15 minutes of the last request. While connected the watch also sends new records about every 15 minutes. The data stays here and fills the Health tab.

column5: Write daily summaries and workouts for other tools
column13: Writes daily.ndjson and activities.ndjson (one JSON record per line) under ~/.config/stoandl/health whenever new data arrives. Nothing is uploaded.

column5: Add steps and heart rate for every minute
column13: One file per day under health/samples; much larger than the summaries.

column5: How many recent days each export rewrites (days)
column13: Picks up late changes, such as sleep the watch finalises later; older days stay as written. Larger values take longer on a slow phone.

column5: Read the watch's hourly battery report
column13: Decodes the watch's hourly diagnostic record (charge, voltage, the watch's own time-to-empty) for the Battery page. Works for classic watches and across disconnects; stays on this device.

column5: Record the level the watch reports over Bluetooth
column13: Records every change while on. The Battery page prefers the hourly report and uses this log when the report can't be read, for example on very new firmware.

column5: Older entries are deleted (days)
column13: Applies to both sources.

column5: Move the watchface you switch to to the top
column13: As in the official app. Off keeps the order you arranged on the Apps tab.

column5: Let watchapps ask for this device's location
column13: Watchapps and faces that ask for your position (navigation, sports, many weather faces) get it from GeoClue: street level, or GPS for apps that ask for high accuracy. Off by default because any app that asks gets your location.

column5: Data and actions from this device that apps can use
column13: Lets watchapps use built-in plugins (weather, music, calendar, phone, watch settings), plugins an app brings, and those extensions offer. Also turns on app permissions. Off by default: no plugin code runs and nothing is fetched.
column16: only the hosts you allow apps to reach

column5: When an app has to ask you before it may use a permission
column13: When data could leave asks before every action and before anything that can send data off this device, but lets an app without a companion app or internet access read without asking. Always also asks before every read. Never grants whatever would need asking; only what you denied stays denied.

column5: Apply permissions to apps made before they existed
column13: Older apps keep internet access and what they declared, so they keep working. On makes them ask like newer apps; some may not work until allowed.

column5: Must match the GeoClue allow rule
column13: The id stoandl gives GeoClue, for both Location for watchapps and current-location weather. Change it only if /etc/geoclue/geoclue.conf allows a different id.

column5: With several watches, connect the one in range
column13: stoandl tries the most recently used watch first and moves on if it is out of range. A working connection is never dropped to switch.

column5: A manual disconnect survives restarts
column13: A watch you disconnect stays disconnected until you connect it again, even across restarts, like the official app.

column5: For Pebble Time, Time Steel and Time Round (experimental)
column13: Classic-era watches connect more reliably over Bluetooth Classic. With this on, pairing also searches for them and they reconnect over Classic; it costs nothing while no such watch is paired.

column5: Save phone battery overnight
column13: During the watch's scheduled Quiet Time, once the screen has been off for 10 minutes, the connection pauses until Quiet Time ends or the screen comes on; notifications from that time are delivered then. If calls may interrupt Quiet Time, the connection stays on.

column3: Hold watch data while the screen is off
column5: Fewer wake-ups; health data arrives later
column13: The watch sends health and app data about every 15 minutes, which wakes a sleeping phone about four times an hour. With this on it keeps the data until the screen is on. Only useful on a phone that stays connected while suspended.

column5: Briefly delay suspend for pending watch traffic
column13: Before suspend, stoandl asks the system to wait until anything on its way to the watch has arrived. It never stops a suspend and releases at once when nothing is pending, so it is harmless on a desktop.

column5: Upper limit per suspend (ms)
column13: The system's own limit is usually 5 s; 0 doesn't wait. Raise it if notifications that wake the phone sometimes only arrive on its next wake.

column5: Pebble 2 Duo and Time 2 updates, from GitHub
column13: Looks for newer PebbleOS releases on GitHub and installs them. Installing a .pbz you already have works without it (Diagnostics & developer → Flash firmware).

column5: Older Pebble updates, from Rebble
column13: The same for classic watches (Pebble, Time, Time Steel, Time Round, Pebble 2).
column16: cohorts.rebble.io, or the update server set under Advanced

column5: Show a message here and on the watch when one exists
column13: Checks when a watch connects, at most once a day, with an Update button. Off: updates are only found when you check yourself.

column5: Also offer beta firmware from GitHub
column13: Earlier fixes and features, possibly new bugs. The newest version with a build for your watch is offered.

column5: Install watch languages from the online catalog
column13: Downloads a pack and installs it on the watch. Installing a .pbl you already have always works.
column16: binaries.rebble.io, or GitHub for community packs

column5: owner/repo that publishes the firmware
column13: Change only to follow a fork that publishes normal_‹board›_‹version›.pbz releases.

column5: Base URL, for a self-hosted mirror
column13: Every classic firmware check asks this server instead of Rebble's.

column5: No password: anyone on your network can install apps
column13: Starts the developer connection (port 9000, all interfaces) whenever a watch connects, so the Pebble SDK and CloudPebble can install and debug apps. Leave off and start it by hand when needed.

column5: Store what watchapps log, for developers
column13: Saves DataLogging data under ~/.config/stoandl/datalog, readable with `stoandl datalog`. A chatty app can fill the disk.
